title: X10 residual: all-day notification dedup only works same-timezone — needs AppPreferences home-timezone field (orchestrator-gated schema change)

description: Flaw: NotificationScheduler resolves an all-day task's default fire time using each device's own TimeZone.current (constructed with .current in both AppEnvironment.swift files), so two devices in different time zones compute different absolute instants for 'the same' all-day reminder and both fire instead of the second suppressing via the lastFiredAt cross-device dedup guard (design doc Section 4 promises 'a few seconds' race window, no all-day carve-out). Limits of the plan-4b interim patch: dedup is correct only when all of a user's devices share the same time zone; cross-timezone concurrent devices legitimately double-fire, pinned by a KNOWN LIMITATION regression test and documented in the design doc as a tracked gap, not intended behavior. Redesign trigger: add a new synced 'home time zone' field to the AppPreferences Core Data entity (NOT per-NotificationSpec/per-Task -- see .council/x10-all-day-timezone-dedup-posture/DECISION.md for why), resolve all-day anchors through it instead of timeZone: .current on both platforms, and expose it as a user-visible Settings affordance. Requires orchestrator (Mikey) approval before any .xcdatamodeld edit -- this is a real data-model change with CloudKit schema implications (Development-to-Production Console deploy needed before Production builds can use the new field). Full council audit trail: .council/x10-all-day-timezone-dedup-posture/DECISION.md. Option (b) (widen the lastFiredAt dedup tolerance window instead) was considered and rejected -- proven mathematically unfixable by the existing deadlineChangeAfterFireReschedules test, which requires the window stay under 24h while realistic timezone deltas need ~24h+ to suppress duplicates.
